Hi all — I took a pass on BrightCorp's redlines. Summary of our position and a proposed compromise attached (RN-NEHA-REDLINE.docx):

1) Defense control: Redwood can accept joint control with primary defense management by Redwood for a third-party IP claim, provided BrightCorp has prior written notice of proposed material settlements and a consent right for settlements that include injunctive relief affecting core service features. If BrightCorp withholds consent unreasonably, Redwood can proceed after 15 business days unless injunctive relief is sought.

2) Scope of indemnity: We will defend and indemnify for third-party claims that allege direct IP infringement by the Redwood service itself (not downstream use). We propose narrowing absolute remedy language to actual, direct damages, plus reasonable defense costs. We are not agreeing to consequential damages for third-party IP claims.

3) Notice & evidence: BrightCorp's request for service-of-record (logs, inputs/outputs) is reasonable in principle. We propose a phased approach: (a) initial notice plus minimal claim summary within 10 business days; (b) Redwood produces service metadata and logs (subject to retention policies and privacy constraints) within 30 days where available; (c) preservation hold obligations for relevant artifacts. We cannot commit to perpetual storage of full model inputs/outputs except where retention was already configured.

4) OSS carveout: we cannot fully accept an open-source carveout that transfers all defense to BrightCorp, but we can accept a limited carveout for claims that arise solely from Customer's modifications to OSS components or Customer-managed open-source stacks.

5) Insurance offset & cap: Redwood proposes a per-claim cap equal to the higher of actual direct damages or $5M, and insurance offsets where applicable. This is negotiable at the enterprise pricing level.

Attached: RN-NEHA-REDLINE.docx (docx) — this is a redline of §10 and §12 with comments.

If BrightCorp is comfortable with the phased evidence timeline and mutual settlement consent, we can finalize the order form quickly. Suggest a 30-minute sync tomorrow at 10:00 PT to settle the last commercial tradeoffs.

—Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference

Kimberly — appreciate the clear read. Daniel and our in-house counsel reviewed your proposed phased evidence timeline. Two follow-ups from BrightCorp:

1) OSS carveout: we would press for a stronger carveout limited to claims brought by licensors of open-source components where BrightCorp has not modified the upstream code. We understand Redwood's concern about downstream misuse; our ask is narrow and tied to upstream OSS licensors.

2) Notice timing for injunctive relief: BrightCorp cannot always provide 15 business days' notice if a third party moves for injunctive relief. We propose a short cooperation/notice requirement (10 business days) plus an obligation on Redwood to provide expedited logs on request if a court process is underway.

We are open to mutual settlement consent language. We also want to ensure that Redwood's proposed $5M cap doesn't undercut BrightCorp's ability to secure remedies if the infringement is commercially material. Can you confirm whether that cap is per claim or aggregate?

I'm attaching our annotated comments to your redline — BrightCorp_comments.docx.

If Redwood's team can take the OSS carveout and provide an explicit "expedited evidence response" clause for injunctive processes, I think we can move to signatures next week.

Thanks,
Lauren
